subject: Chemistry
title: SN2 Mechanism: Backside Attack and Walden Inversion
summary: SN2 = Substitution, Nucleophilic, bimolecular: one step in which the nucleophile enters from the back as the halide leaves. In this lesson: rate = k[CH3Cl][OH-] (second order), backside attack at 180°, one step through the transition state with partial bonds and three H in one plane, Walden inversion (like an umbrella turning inside out), reactivity CH3X ＞ 1° ＞ 2° ＞ 3°, and two solved questions including (R)-2-bromobutane → (S)-butan-2-ol.

notes.title: SN2 Mechanism
notes.blurb: reaction and rate law, the mechanism (one step), reactivity, stereochemistry

keyPoints: **SN2**: **One step**, second order. S, N, 2 = substitution, nucleophilic, **bimolecular**.
**Backside attack**: The front is **blocked** by X. Transition state: **partial bonds**, 3 groups in a plane.
**Walden inversion**: Configuration is **inverted**. Label may change: check **priorities**.

blocks.p: CH₃Cl + OH⁻ → CH₃OH + Cl⁻ · rate = k [CH₃Cl] [OH⁻] (second order)
Doubling both concentrations makes the reaction four times faster. (Hughes and Ingold proposed the mechanism in 1937.)

list: **Backside attack:** the nucleophile approaches the carbon from the side opposite the halogen (180°), because the large, electron-rich halogen blocks the front.
**Transition state:** the C–OH bond is half formed and the C–Cl bond half broken (partial bonds); the three hydrogens lie in one plane; the carbon is momentarily bonded to five groups.
**Inversion:** as Cl⁻ leaves, the three groups flip to the other side, like an umbrella turning inside out in the wind: **inversion of configuration (Walden inversion)**.

blocks.p: The backside must be accessible, so steric hindrance decides the rate: **CH₃X > 1° > 2° > 3°**. Tertiary halides hardly react by SN2. For the same alkyl group, R–I > R–Br > R–Cl (leaving-group ability).

An optically active substrate gives a product of inverted configuration. Whether the R/S label changes depends on the priorities: for (R)-2-bromobutane + OH⁻ (SN2), OH takes the place of Br at the same priority rank, so the product is **(S)-butan-2-ol**.

list: ✗ SN2 is first order (it is second order).
✗ Inversion always changes R to S (only when the priority order is unchanged).
✗ 3° halides react fastest by SN2 (they react slowest).

blocks.p: **Q1.** 1-bromobutane (1°, less crowded) reacts faster than 2-bromobutane by SN2.

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: Statement I: High concentration of strong nucleophilic reagent with secondary alkyl halides which do not have bulky substituents will follow SN2 mechanism. Statement II: A secondary alkyl halide when treated with a large excess of ethanol follows SN1 mechanism.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both statement I and Statement II are false.
Both statement I and Statement II are true.
pyq.explain: A strong nucleophile at high concentration with an unhindered 2° halide favours SN2; a large excess of a weak nucleophile / polar protic solvent (ethanol) favours SN1 (solvolysis).
